topic: Retry Storms Vaporize Half-Open Circuit Breakers
postText:
Your core service crashes. Circuit breaker trips open. System breathes, but real disaster strikes exact second recovery begins.

In healthcare IT handling telemetry and patient intake, downstream APIs face transient saturation. Breaker opens correctly to protect database connections. Downstream recovers. Breaker enters Half-Open state, sending limited probe requests to verify health.

Then instant failure occurs.

Thousands of client instances, queued background tasks, and unjittered mobile apps all retry concurrently. Aggressive retries slam the API Gateway. Incoming wave swamps downstream before probe completes. Probe times out. Breaker marks downstream dead and flips Open again. Repeat loop forever. System oscillates in permanent self-inflicted outage.

Three fixes prevent this thrashing:

1. Enforce Retry Budgets at Edge Gateway: Discard retries if retry ratio exceeds 10% of total incoming requests.
2. Implement Full Jitter: Sleep formula must use random uniform distribution up to base exponential backoff. Spreads aggregate demand curve.
3. Dedicated Canary Channels: Half-open validation probes must use isolated, reserved network channels bypass-throttled away from normal retry floods.

Without strict rate limiting on retry attempts, your resilience mechanisms generate the exact load that destroys them.
